findings.title: Interpolating before split-support check defeats $__range split protection
findings.body: `applyTemplateVariables` is called before `partition(queries, ... querySupportsSplitting)`. `querySupportsSplitting` deliberately excludes queries containing `$__range` via `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` because split sub-requests would otherwise use the full range duration rather than the sub-range. After frontend interpolation, any `$__range` token in the expression is replaced with the full request range duration, so `isQueryWithRangeVariable` no longer sees it and the query is split, producing incorrect results for each sub-request. The check must use the original (pre-interpolation) expression or preserve the raw expression for this test.

findings.title: Sharded queries are template-interpolated twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates each target via `applyTemplateVariables` and passes the already interpolated `queries` to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. Inside that function, each shard group is executed via `runSplitQuery`, which on line 299 of querySplitting.ts again applies `applyTemplateVariables` to its targets. This double interpolation is redundant and can produce incorrect expressions if a template variable resolves to a string containing another variable placeholder. The test change to expect `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single target confirms this behavior. Interpolation should happen only once or `runSplitQuery` should skip interpolation when targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: Filtering by expr before interpolation can include queries that become empty
findings.body: Previously `interpolateVariablesInQueries` was called before `.filter((query) => query.expr)`, so a query whose expression contained a template variable that resolved to an empty string was filtered out. Now filtering occurs before `applyTemplateVariables`; if interpolation yields an empty `expr`, the query remains in the target list and will be sent to Loki as an empty expression, likely causing a query error. The filter should be applied after interpolation or additionally check the interpolated expression.
